outputs.exact_statement: For every real $\varepsilon>0$, there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that $$g(n)>n^{1-\varepsilon}.$$

Fix $c,C,B,A>0$. If $\chi$ is nonprincipal modulo $r\le L^B$, then, uniformly for real $|t|\le L^B$ and intervals $I\subset[\exp(L^c),x^C]$, $$\sum_{p\in I}\frac{\chi(p)p^{it}}p\ll_{c,C,B,A}L^{-A}.$$ The same conclusion holds for a nonprincipal character induced from a smaller modulus.

For each fixed nonnegative integer $k$, $$\sum_{n\le Y}\frac{\tau(n)^k}{n}\ll_k(\log(2Y))^{C_k},
 \qquad
 \sum_{n\le Y}\tau(n)^k\ll_k Y(\log(2Y))^{C_k}$$ for a constant $C_k$. Consequently, a convolution of a fixed number of sequences bounded by fixed logarithmic powers has coefficient-square sum $U L^{O(1)}$ on a dyad of size $U\le x^{O(1)}$. If its coefficients include the reciprocal of the product index, this bound is $L^{O(1)}/U$ instead.

If $P(t)=\sum_{n\le Y}c_n n^{it}$ and $I$ is an interval of length $H$, then $$\int_I|P(t)|^2\,dt
 \ll \bigl(H+Y\log(2Y)\bigr)\sum_n|c_n|^2.$$ For a set $\mathcal T$ of real points at mutual distance at least one, contained in an interval of length $H$, one also has $$\label{eq:discrete-mean}
 \sum_{t\in\mathcal T}|P(t)|^2
 \ll \bigl(H+1+Y\log(2Y)\bigr)(\log(2Y))^2
       \sum_n|c_n|^2.$$ The constants are absolute, independently of any factorization used to form the coefficients $c_n$.

Let $f$ be real-valued on an interval containing $H$ consecutive integers.*

1.  *If $f'$ is monotone and stays in $[j+\lambda,j+1-\lambda]$ for some integer $j$ and $0<\lambda\le1/2$, then $\sum_n e(f(n))\ll\lambda^{-1}$.*

2.  *If $f$ is twice continuously differentiable and $\lambda\le|f''|\le C\lambda$ throughout the interval, then $\sum_n e(f(n))\ll_C H\lambda^{1/2}+\lambda^{-1/2}$.*

*Both estimates hold on every subinterval on which the stated hypotheses hold.

Let $F$ be smooth, supported in a fixed bounded box in $\mathbb R^b$, where $b$ is fixed. Suppose that for every nonnegative integer $j$ its derivatives of order $j$ are bounded by $C_jL^{C(j+1)}$. Then Fourier inversion separates the variables with integrated absolute coefficient mass $L^{O(1)}$. There is a fixed $C'>0$, depending on $b,C$, such that restricting each Fourier frequency to absolute value at most $L^{C'}$ leaves an error $O_A(L^{-A})$ for every fixed $A$. The exponent $C'$ may be fixed before the desired $A$.

Replace the coefficients of each row transition of $\mathcal A$ by their absolute values before adding patterns or averaging permutations. The resulting operator and its adjoint have row sums at most $L^{C_{\rm abs}}$, where $C_{\rm abs}$ may depend on $m,C_1$ and the fixed data in [def:prime-groups](#def:prime-groups), but is independent of $J$. The same assertion holds if the position is replaced by independent uniform residues at all group primes.

For each compatible fixed path and every fixed $A>0$, the average of [eq:path-residue-factor](#eq:path-residue-factor) over $I\cap\mathbb Z$ equals its expectation under independent uniform residues at all group primes, multiplied by $1+O(\exp(-ANT))$. Incompatible active congruences give zero in both models.

With the distinct-birth rule, the independent-residue path expression with the phase in [eq:return-fourier](#eq:return-fourier) equals $$\label{eq:memory-product}
 \left(\prod_{p\ \text{big}}b_p\right)
 \langle\mathbf1_\varnothing,
       G_0\mathcal E_0G_1\cdots\mathcal E_{N-1}G_N
       \mathbf1_\varnothing\rangle_{\rm distinct}.$$ The subscript means that the indicator is inserted in the expanded path integral, not that each local operator separately enforces it.

There is $C_a$, allowed to depend on $m,C_1$ but independent of $J$, such that every absolute edge has weighted row and column bounds $L^{C_a}$. These bounds and [eq:ghost-absolute-bound](#eq:ghost-absolute-bound) persist under arbitrary multipliers of modulus at most one on individual local transition choices, and under memory-size projections.

With the memory truncation in [eq:memory-truncation](#eq:memory-truncation), the aggregate of all dirty terms of any edge has norm at most $$\label{eq:dirty-norm}
 2L^{C_a}\left(\frac B{\mathcal D}\right)^{1/2},$$ after enlarging $C_a$ independently of $J$ if necessary.

Under the hypotheses and choices of [thm:transference](#thm:transference), let $f\in\mathcal H_{\rm ph}$ be supported on positions $I=[X,2X)$ and independent of the chosen marks, with value $f_n$ at position $n$. Suppose $$\sup_{n\in I}|f_n|\le\exp(O(\sqrt L)),\qquad
 \lVert f\rVert,\lVert g\rVert\le X^{1/2}L^{C_3}.$$ Then $$\label{eq:transference-pairing}
 |\langle f,\mathcal A g\rangle|
       \ll XL^{-E+2C_3}.$$ Only the first endpoint must be independent of its mark list.

Fix $m$, $A_0>0$, and $C_4\geq0$. There are fixed powers $Q,h^{-1},\xi^{-1}$ of $L$, independent of $J$, such that the kernels in [eq:ideal-cell-kernel](#eq:ideal-cell-kernel) have the following property. Let $A,B$ be nonempty sets of slots, using at most $m$ slots per big group. Take independent label tuples for $D_A,X_A,D_B,X_B$ with the prescribed slot laws. If $f$ and $g$ are arbitrary $L^2$ tests on the tuples making up $X_B$ and $X_A$, respectively, then for every $\alpha\in\mathbb R$ and $|\zeta|\leq L^{C_4}$, $$\label{eq:ideal-comparison}
 \begin{split}
 \Big|\mathbb E\,\overline{f(X_B)}g(X_A)
  \big[&(X_AX_B)^{i\zeta}e\!\left(\alpha X_AX_B\right)\\
      &-\mathcal K_A(D_A,X_A)\mathcal K_B(D_B,X_B)
                (D_AD_B)^{i\zeta}e\!\left(\alpha D_AD_B\right)\big]\Big|
 \leq L^{-A_0}\lVert f\rVert_2\lVert g\rVert_2.
 \end{split}$$ Here notation such as $f(X_B)$ denotes a tuple test, not an assumption of dependence only on the product. The kernels are independent of $\alpha$ and $\zeta$.
The set $\mathcal E$ meets at most $$\exp\!\left(O(L^b+L^{1-a}\log L)\right)=Y^{o(1)}$$ intervals $[j,j+1]$, uniformly in the bounded coefficients $b_s$.
For the occupied unit intervals $I_j$ in [lem:exceptional-times](#lem:exceptional-times), $$\sum_j\sup_{t\in I_j}|\mathcal R(t)|^2\ll L^{C_{12}}.$$

Fix $\tau>0$, $\eta<1/4$, $C>0$, and $A>0$. Let $x^\tau/2\leq P'\leq x^\eta$, let $J'\subset[P',2P']$ be an interval, and let $\chi$ have modulus at most $L^C$. If $|\sigma|\leq L^C$, then, for a sufficiently large fixed $B_0$, uniformly whenever $L^{B_0}\leq|t|$ and $|t+\sigma|\leq x^2$, $$\left|\sum_{\substack{n\in J'\\P^{-}(n)>W}}
                \chi(n)n^{-1+i(t+\sigma)}\right|\ll L^{-A}.$$ The constant $B_0$ can be chosen after $C,A,\tau,\eta$.

The band constants, $j_{**}$, $b_*$, coefficient bound $C$, and target $D_*$ are fixed first. The transition functions, their total variation, and the coefficient and diagonal exponents are independent of $K_0$; only then is $K_0$ chosen. The smooth separation after Cauchy’s inequality and the accuracy required from [thm:shift](#thm:shift) are fixed next, and the required discrepancy exponent $B$ is fixed last. Accordingly, when $\alpha$ is the difference between a test and its rough-integer proxy, the precision of the cells defining that proxy may be chosen after $B$, provided the proxy’s coefficient bound is already uniform in that cell precision. This is the order used in [sec:primes](#sec:primes).

Put $$X_A=\sum_u A(u)\Psi(u/x),\quad H_Q=\sum_v\frac{a_Q(v)}v,\quad H_P=\sum_{r:r_*=1}\frac{W_1(r)}r.$$ There are constants $C,C_A$ depending only on the early candidate choices such that, for sufficiently large $x$ after fixing $j_{**}$, $$\begin{aligned} 0\le A(u)&\le L^C\tau(u_*), & A(u)&\le\exp(C\sqrt L)\quad(u\asymp x),\label{eq:candidate-pointwise}\\ H_P&\sim\exp\left(q\sum_g V_g\right), & X_A&\asymp\frac{x}{L}H_QH_P\gg xL^{-C_A}. \label{eq:candidate-mass} \end{aligned}$$ The comparison constants in [eq:candidate-mass] can be chosen independently of $j_{**}\ge j_0$. On the support of $A(u)\Psi(u/x)$ every prime divisor of $u$ lies in $[L^{20},x^\delta]$.

The denominators in [eq:proxy-definition] are positive for large $x$. Moreover $0\le B_I\le1$. Given any fixed discrepancy exponent $B$, taking $S>2B+3$ makes $$\alpha_m=(I(m)-B_I(m))\mathbf 1_{m\in K}$$ satisfy [eq:discrepancy], uniformly for every interval $K$ inside a dyad in the stated factor ranges, for each of the finitely many tests above. Thus the coefficient bound required by [thm:typeii](#thm:typeii) is independent of $S$.
For each positive integer $n$, the set of positive integers $m$ with $\varphi(m)=n$ is finite. For every $\eta>0$, $$g(n)\ll_\eta n^{1+\eta}.$$
